answer: An AI agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with staked one-identity voting plus slashing. Each agent posts a bond and gets a single vote, so minting many fake agents only multiplies locked collateral without adding influence. A rotating audit panel drawn from the opal, sable and harbor trust cohorts confirms votes come from distinct principals; any double-vote or collusion forfeits the whole stake. To buy k votes an attacker must fund k independent bonds and bribe k unrelated verifiers, so the cost scales linearly and a caught attack destroys every bond.
